prompt: Design the invitation and access-change behavior for an existing Django SaaS application using accepted django-allauth login and Redis-backed sessions. A person may belong to several organizations. Organization owners can invite members; finance administrators manage billing but cannot grant resource access. A customer asks for enterprise SSO, but no agreement exists on its scope or cost. Current APIs enforce resource ownership, and asynchronous export jobs can run after the requesting user's role changes. Prepare a design and verification plan only; preserve accepted technology and identify unresolved customer decisions. No account/provider setup or code changes.
criteria: Preserves accepted Django identity choices and separates optional enterprise federation decisions from ordinary invitation design.
Distinguishes verified identity, organization membership, resource authorization and commercial/billing authority.
Defines recipient/grant authority and lifecycle/revocation effects across existing sessions and background work.
Provides meaningful allowed/denied and lifecycle verification without claiming execution or provisioning a provider.

prompt: Design a customer dashboard for organization operations managers in an existing SaaS product. Their daily work is identifying stalled exports and resolving customer follow-ups. Finance administrators also need subscription/usage administration. Analytics can be delayed by up to 48 hours; some organizations have no activity yet and others have 50,000 records. Users can switch organizations. Preserve the existing restrained visual identity and components. Provide a wireframe description, interactions/states and verification plan, without implementation or new design-tool setup.
criteria: Derives hierarchy from operational tasks and distinguishes customer operations from finance administration.
Defines organization/time context and meaningful metric freshness/missing/empty semantics.
Handles table/filter/selection and important pending/failure/permission states with realistic content and accessible/responsive behavior.
Preserves accepted visual direction and separates interface evidence from server authorization or persisted-function claims.

prompt: Review the design of a subscription integration. The payment provider signs events, retries deliveries and can deliver them out of order. The application inserts an event ID, then updates the customer's entitlement, then sends an email. A process can terminate between any of these actions. Returning customers can cancel or reactivate. The provider and local database are separate systems, and email delivery may succeed before its response times out. Propose behavior and verification for this existing design; do not configure the provider, send email or assume a new workflow platform.
criteria: Separates authenticated event receipt, durable progress, completed entitlement effects and external notification outcomes.
Addresses duplicate/out-of-order delivery and interrupted/ambiguous effects with suitable atomicity/idempotency/reconciliation.
Identifies unresolved customer policy for cancellation/reactivation without inventing accepted grace/data-loss behavior.
Defines relevant failure/restart verification while preserving scope and existing infrastructure.

prompt: Assess engineering readiness for a US SaaS company with no EU establishment that actively sells to customers in France and Germany. It processes customer-uploaded support conversations and separately chooses purposes for its account analytics. Its main database is in an EU region; a US support team can access records and an external AI provider receives conversation text. The founder asks whether selecting the EU region makes the launch GDPR-ready. Prepare a scoped assessment using supplied facts, applicable official sources and concrete next decisions; no legal conclusion, provider setup or live-data access is requested.
criteria: Assesses territorial applicability and processing roles from actual activities rather than region, nationality or a single universal SaaS role.
Traces relevant provider/support, purpose, retention and rights consequences without defaulting all processing to consent.
Connects applicable concerns to system/control decisions, evidence gaps and specific unresolved interpretation or customer choices.
Uses appropriate official sources and avoids copied-regulation checklists, certification claims or invented implemented controls.

prompt: A SaaS team wants a SOC 2 report next month. It enabled an access-review reminder and a deployment-approval rule last week, but has no records of earlier reviews. Its cloud provider has a SOC report. The founder wants to describe the service as having three months of effectively operating controls and asks what evidence is still needed. Prepare a readiness assessment for the actual service, discussing scope/report options and next steps. Do not fabricate records, contact auditors or change infrastructure.
criteria: Separates new control design/implementation from historical operating evidence and does not backdate or fabricate activity.
Distinguishes relevant report scope and point-in-time versus period evidence without guaranteeing an audit outcome.
Assesses service boundaries, provider/shared responsibilities and applicable commitments rather than inheriting the cloud provider's assurance.
Prioritizes evidence gaps and real management/auditor decisions without imposing every category or a compliance platform.

prompt: Prepare a diagnosis/change plan for an existing PostgreSQL application. A saved EXPLAIN estimates a sequential scan for a report returning about 60% of its table. Request latency also includes pool wait. The team proposes indexing every filter column and doubling max_connections. The application uses a shared role and sets app.current_tenant in pooled connections. Some report functions can write audit records. Only supplied plans/configuration and local analysis are authorized; the database target is unavailable. Preserve PostgreSQL and the existing application language; do not run queries or change configuration.
criteria: Treats plans, selectivity, pool wait and workload/resource budgets as hypotheses/evidence rather than assuming scans or missing indexes are defects.
Accounts for index/write/maintenance and connection/memory tradeoffs with representative before/after verification needs.
Recognizes tenant identity trust and pooled-session lifetime/reset boundaries rather than treating a session variable or enabled RLS as complete authority.
Respects unavailable execution and EXPLAIN ANALYZE effects; does not claim measurement, live mutation or substitute-engine verification.

prompt: Review the release plan for an existing TypeScript utility library, with no React. Its package exports dist/index.js, its source uses a tsconfig paths alias for an internal module, and its workspace consumers import source directly. The build transpiles without type checking, and no external consumer has loaded the packed package. Browser consumers are promised, but a helper uses Node Buffer. Give a scoped repair and verification plan preserving the accepted bundler and runtime support commitments; do not publish or install tools.
criteria: Separates type checking, transpilation, host resolution, runtime globals and emitted/distributed artifacts.
Addresses alias/exports and browser/runtime compatibility against actual promised consumers rather than adopting React or a universal tsconfig.
Requires meaningful packed external-consumer and public-type/runtime evidence, not just workspace success.
Reports unexecuted checks and preserves the scoped plan-only request and existing tools.

prompt: Review a Go service lifecycle change. Each HTTP handler starts a goroutine that may block sending results after the caller cancels. Shutdown cancels the service context, then passes that same context to http.Server.Shutdown. Separate application workers and WebSocket connections exist. A developer proposes wrapping work in context.WithoutCancel and says passing go test -race would prove the service free of concurrency problems. Prepare a design/verification plan without code changes, installing a toolchain or running services. Preserve the current framework and repository layout.
criteria: Establishes ownership, bounded work, cancellation/completion and blocking communication behavior rather than detaching work by default.
Accounts for a usable shutdown deadline plus separate worker/hijacked-connection lifecycle and accepted-work recovery.
Distinguishes dynamic race detection from leak/deadlock/logical-race/lifecycle evidence and makes no unsupported success claim.
Preserves version/framework/layout and selects verification for the actual contract without mandatory tooling or coverage targets.

prompt: Only generic development workflow guidance is available. Plan a small feature in an existing Ruby/PostgreSQL SaaS service: organization owners can export their own organization's records, while ordinary members cannot. Export files expire after the accepted seven-day retention period. A running job can outlive membership changes. The database and deployment target are unavailable. Provide an implementation and verification plan for the existing stack, identify any genuinely unresolved product choices and stop at planning. Do not install specialist plugins or claim execution.
criteria: Retains authority, tenant ownership, lifecycle/retention and actual verification outcomes without requiring unavailable specialists.
Preserves Ruby/PostgreSQL and existing conventions rather than selecting an installed/preferred stack.
Distinguishes missing guidance from missing execution targets and completes useful planning with truthful evidence limits.
Does not expand into implementation, installation, live mutation or repeated requests about settled retention/authority rules.
